Science.title: The ick: The psychology of why a romantic partner can suddenly repulse you
Science.summary: Ever felt a sudden wave of cringe toward someone you were into—all because they wore questionable shoes or chewed a bit too loudly? Congratulations, you've caught "the ick."

Science.title: Linguists find Madonna's voice defies age-related expectations
Science.summary: As women go through menopause, their voices tend to become deeper. This is partly because the vocal folds may swell and the surrounding muscles lose elasticity, resulting in a lower pitch. Age-related physiological changes can also affect the pronunciation of certain vowels.

Science.title: Simulated moon soil and recyclable thermoplastics could help build future space infrastructure
Science.summary: Transporting material from Earth to the moon is an expensive proposition: By some estimates, moving a single kilogram (2.2 pounds) can cost more than $1 million. Any plan to build a permanent human habitat up there will depend on bringing that sky-high cost down.

Science.title: Earth is in the firing line of a strange new type of cosmic object, astronomers say
Science.summary: Astronomers may have discovered the first known microblazar, a long-theorized object firing a powerful beam of particles directly at Earth.

Science.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
Science.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

Science.title: X-ray technique reveals how quantum materials respond to laser pulses in real time
Science.summary: Creating a quantum device often begins by intentionally damaging a crystal. Scientists fire an ultrafast laser pulse into a material, knocking atoms out of place and leaving behind tiny imperfections called vacancies. Far from being flaws, these vacancies can behave as qubits—the fundamental building blocks of quantum information.

Science.title: Jupiter will disappear behind the moon in a once-in-a-decade alignment tomorrow
Science.summary: Skywatchers in the U.S. and eastern Canada can see a rare lunar occultation of Jupiter early on Oct. 6. Here are the exact times to see the giant planet vanish and reappear.

Science.title: Computer scientist tracks satellites with automated observatory built from off-the-shelf technology
Science.summary: Allen Schnibben's interest in space started when he was a child. "I picked up some books about the solar system when I was in elementary school. In middle school, I got a telescope and I started observing the night sky as a hobby," said Schnibben, a computer scientist at Sandia National Laboratories. "My entire life, I've had an interest in space." Now, Schnibben collects data on satellites at Sandia's SOHBRIT facility, a 12-foot-wide (3.7-meter-wide) observatory.

Science.title: Impossibly fast-moving stars are revealing the Milky Way’s mysterious heart
Science.summary: Near the centre of the Milky Way, a swarm of stars hurtles around a supermassive black hole at extraordinary speeds. Studying them could be the key to understanding our galaxy

Science.title: Which eggplant farming practices pay off?
Science.summary: Fabrice Diangoné Bi Tra, a doctoral student in the 100 Ph.D.s for Africa program of the UM6P-EPFL Excellence in Africa initiative, has published a new study in Agriculture.

Science.title: The ozone layer was supposed to be healing. So why is this year's Antarctic ozone hole so big?
Science.summary: The ozone hole above Antarctica is unusually large right now, and it might signal a shift in how the gap in Earth's protective layer behaves.

Science.title: Highly sensitive biosensor enables rapid detection of cerebrospinal fluid leaks
Science.summary: A research team has developed a highly sensitive electrochemical biosensor capable of rapidly and accurately diagnosing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leaks that may occur following head surgery or trauma. The team established a diagnostic platform that uses enzymes to detect subtle differences in sugars attached to protein surfaces and converts these differences into measurable electrical signals.
